topics.topic_label: Enterprise agent platforms (AWS closes Bedrock Agents to new customers and renames it Classic — the first hyperscaler agent framework to reach end-of-life, in under three years; Oracle puts Gemini 3.1/3.5 Flash inside Fusion, NetSuite and AI Agent Studio; Cloudflare opens Agents Week by naming zero products)

Vendor governance as a business line (Cequence ships AI Discovery plus API, LLM and Skill registries that find shadow agents and MCP servers by mining security logs; 'a fully populated audit trail is not evidence that review happened'; Hardoon works the arithmetic against questionnaire-based governance at fleet scale)

Implementation & deployment revenue (Unique AI hires a Team Lead for an already-existing Global Forward Deployed Data Science team, with staffing responsibility and 1:1s — FDE acquires a management layer; Thinking Machines' open-model finetuning service reportedly does hundreds of millions in annual revenue)

Evaluation gap (an 'always positive' policy scores 0.690 on R-Judge above five models that genuinely discriminate, and the three broad safety benchmarks rank the same 18 models differently; a failure taxonomy reframes repair as an assignment problem; financial-institution validators argue benchmark scores are not approval evidence)

Enterprise agent platforms (AWS puts Superblocks inside customer VPCs to kill shadow IT; Stripe's company-wide Kai agent live in one week on Deep Agents; Deutsche Telekom's LMOS agentic-compute layer)

Governance as a product line (SonarSource sells 'AI code verification and governance' and is hiring engineers to build circuit breakers, sandboxes and trust telemetry — governance hired for as product engineering, not compliance; AISPA audits 3,249 system-prompt instructions across 88 commercial products; BaFin gains AI supervision over banks and insurers)

Implementation & services revenue (the interesting number in the Stripe case study is the week, not the architecture — most enterprise agent programmes are measured in quarters because they start by building the harness; Forward Deployed Engineering acquires an Executive Director layer and Glassdoor's Swiss FDE count moves 24 → 40)

Evaluation gap (an 'always positive' policy scores F1 0.690 on R-Judge, beating five of 21 discriminating models, and capability correlates negatively with safety scores; a 257-paper synthesis finds temporal, regulatory and multi-agent assurance immature; HN's best-argued critique is a missing denominator)

Governance as a product line (an ex-Deloitte auditor open-sources the whole SOC 2 method aimed at AI products — the best-performing Show HN of the day; Julius Baer hires an architect whose deliverable is Architecture Decision Records approved at architecture boards; NetHope ships a pre-adoption PESTLE due-diligence guide)

Implementation & services revenue (the number that matters in the CX write-up is organisational, not architectural — configurable agents initialised from a JSON config plus a domain expert's prompt took build time from ~6 months to ~2 weeks, after which 'the platform was no longer the primary constraint; prompt and evaluation quality were')

Governance as a product line (Anaconda's second acquisition in three weeks buys pre-deployment red-teaming, runtime guardrails and NIST/EU-AI-Act compliance automation — governance bolted onto a distribution platform rather than sold as a service; Stanford's AI Index supplies the demand curve, AI-specific governance roles up 17% and firms with no responsible-AI policy down from 24% to 11%, with implementation still blocked by knowledge gaps at 59%)

Implementation & services revenue (the labour side of the trade shows up in the Swiss job file — the forward-deployed-engineer title has spanned Team Lead to zero-years-required inside one country in one week, and the newest posting names no LLM, RAG, prompt or agent requirement at all, listing Claude and Gemini in the benefits stack beside Kubernetes and Postgres)
